newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil trade lacklustre.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil trade lacklustre.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps were largely unaffected by the launch of the Singapore International Monetary Exchange's (SIMEX) futures fuel oil contract, brokers said on Tuesday.
"It is difficult to tell," said one broker. "The market was already very dull yesterday."
Brokers said no fuel oil swaps have been traded so far on Tuesday, with levels just edging up with crude.
May fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $97.75/$98.50 per tonne, from $97.50/$98.50 on Monday. June was quoted at $96.75/$97.50.
In comparison, on its first day of trading, the SIMEX contract for June traded 190 lots and was last quoted at $97.50/$98.00 per tonne.
Gas oil swaps were stable with May quoted at $25.85/$25.95 per barrel, and traded at $25.95. The May/June spread was also traded at $1.40 in backwardation.
Brokers said the Singapore trader who has bought a total of over 14 million barrels of physical gas oil since early March is still expected to bid later on Tuesday.
"On the back of that, paper sellers will hold their position," a broker said.
